svg.text: My master's research at IG-UNICAMP: can a cheap camera catch the moment a
vegetated slope on the Serra do Mar starts moving? An OpenCV pipeline runs
frame by frame on a plain CPU: Gaussian blur, Canny edges and morphological
closing, a circularity filter to find the 40mm target balls, and nearest
distance tracking with a 4px search lock so targets do not get swapped when
something blocks the view. As an independent check, Meta SAM 2 runs zero shot
over the same footage every 30 seconds, DBSCAN groups its masks and a separate
script scores them against ground truth, on a day and a night series. The
notebooks run locally or on Colab, and 19 of the 889 recorded videos are
public. Size is what makes it plausible in the field: 30 minutes of video is
113MB, the target coordinates come down to about 20MB of CSV. One site and a
limited set of runs, so it argues for feasibility, not much more.
